text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: High severity alert - decode-stream-prod cluster - repeated CUDA OOM during streaming decode (node decode-runner-3). Alert count: 92 in the last 5m. @sre-liz @eng-ryan please acknowledge

sre-liz: on it. paging into #incidents for visibility. pulling recent logs and request ids.

eng-ryan: ack. I'm looking at telemetry, seeing a spike in token output for a handful of client keys — looks like a runaway generation pattern, many requests exceeding max_tokens override header.

infra-bot: autoscaler attempted to spin additional pods, one recovered, decode-runner-3 went into CrashLoopBackOff after kernel OOM. Recorded kernel message: `CUDA error: out of memory`

jamal: paste of tail logs from decode-runner-3: ```2026-02-12T20:41:12Z ERROR decode_loop.cpp:412 CUDA out of memory: attempted to allocate 1.2 GiB
2026-02-12T20:41:13Z ERROR runtime: uncaught exception, killing container
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File \"/app/serve/decode.py\", line 198, in _generate
    tokens = model.decode_step(...)
  File \"/opt/rt/runtime/ops.cu\", line 1023, in decode_step
    throw std::runtime_error(\"CUDA OOM\")
```

support-sam: customer ops alert queued for the top 3 clients by request volume (client_ids: c_91, c_24, c_77). CS is prepping comms; ETA 20m for an initial update. Any immediate mitigation to reduce dropped requests?

eng-ryan: two mitigation levers: 1) enforce max_tokens per-API-key at edge (fast) 2) patch runtime to early-reject token headers exceeding model profile (slower). I'll push 1) as hotpatch.

ops-jen: I'll apply a temporary WAF rule to block requests with header `X-Max-Tokens` > 1024 for the affected clients. Doing a scoped rule for client_ids c_91,c_24,c_77 only.

infra-bot: action taken: WAF rule applied (rule id: waf-2319). Blocking 1,042 requests in last 2m matching rule. :white_check_mark:

sre-liz: meanwhile I'm cordoning decode-runner-3 and draining. spinning a replacement pod. `kubectl cordon decode-runner-3 && kubectl drain decode-runner-3 --ignore-daemonsets`

jamal: replacement pod started but reporting high GPU memory usage on startup for the same workload. telemetry: median generation tokens for affected requests ~ 18,432 tokens (expected 512).

eng-ryan: that confirms runaway generation. Root cause likely a malformed client override or proxy mis-mapping header -> body param. I'll trace gateway code path.

support-sam: Customer impact: preliminary count 3.2k requests dropped in last 10m, about 0.6% of total traffic. Two customers (c_91, c_24) reported timeouts. CS recommends offering SLA credit if confirmed revenue impact.

ops-jen: hotpatch note: applying token cap at edge for those keys only avoids global perf hit. Rolling out now to edge shard e-3.

eng-ryan: pushing a quick runtime guard: if requested_max_tokens > model_max_tokens * 4 then early-reject with 400 + guidance. Code snippet I'm about to push: ```if (req.max_tokens > model_profile.max_tokens * 4) { return error(400, \"requested max_tokens exceeds allowed cap; contact support or reduce max_tokens\"); }```

infra-bot: runtime patch deployed to canary (decode-canary-1). Observed canary rejecting large requests. No regressions so far.

sre-liz: oncall handoff in 15m. Current status: WAF hotpatch applied, runtime canary guard deployed, problematic clients scoped and rate-limited. Requests dropping still for old in-flight sessions — working to surface which requests to retry vs lost.

jamal: note: KV cache growth spike correlated — some requests appending long suffixes repeatedly. Telemetry snippet: `avg_kv_cache_entries_per_session: 12 -> 3,400` for affected client keys. This caused memory pressure even before decode loop.

eng-ryan: followup action: we'll add a background eviction policy for excessively long KV histories and a hard cap per-session. I'll open PR for eviction + telemetry alert thresholds.

support-sam: CS asked for quick customer-facing summary. Draft: \"We observed anomalous request patterns causing GPU OOMs and dropped requests; we've implemented immediate rate limits and edge caps for affected clients and are working on permanent runtime guards. We'll follow up with remediation details and credits if needed.\"

sre-liz: good. I'll include confirmed numbers in the incident report. Also flagging incident for postmortem. Triage severity: Sev2 -> may escalate if we see recurrence after mitigations removed.

eng-ryan: found a probable misroute in gateway mapping: when header `X-Stream-Mode: alternate` present, the header parser ignored `max_tokens` and defaulted to unlimited in an older path. Filing issue: GATEWAY-1422.

ops-jen: queued a rolling restart of edge proxies to pick up hotpatch config. Doing 1/3 at a time. Monitoring error rate.

pagerduty-bot: On-call handoff: @sre-liz -> @eng-ryan at 2993337890. Please acknowledge within 5m.

eng-ryan: ack handoff. I will take primary incident lead. Leaving notes for night shift: monitor GPU OOM rate, WAF hits, and `avg_kv_cache_entries_per_session`.

sre-liz: handing off Slack and runbook. Key next steps: consolidate telemetry for dropped req IDs, finalize customer list, merge eviction PR, and schedule postmortem.

support-sam: CS team set to notify impacted customers with the drafted summary. We'll escalate privately for top-tier accounts.

infra-bot: telemetry update: GPU OOMs dropped from 45/min -> 3/min after edge caps. Request drops reduced from 620/min -> 18/min.

eng-ryan: rolling back temporary WAF only after runtime guard is promoted from canary -> prod. ETA 40m for full rollout if canary stays healthy.

sre-liz: signing off from active ops. leaving incident channel open for followups. :wave:

jamal: adding final note: evidence suggests combination of header misparse + customer-side SDK bug that retries with ever-increasing max_tokens. Recommending we contact top customers with suggested client SDK patch.

pagerduty-bot: Incident status updated to \"mitigated\" at 2993337912. Follow-up tasks created: INCIDENT-6984 (postmortem), GATEWAY-1422 (header parser fix), RUNTIME-4551 (KV eviction), and CS-notif-314.
